title: Rivian third-quarter earnings beat estimates as software revenue, R2 deliveries rise
description: Signage outside Rivian's offices in Palo Alto, California, Dec. 10, 2025.Jason Henry | Bloomberg | Getty ImagesRivian Automotive beat Wall Street's th
body: Signage outside Rivian's offices in Palo Alto, California, Dec. 10, 2025.Jason Henry | Bloomberg | Getty ImagesRivian Automotive beat Wall Street's third-quarter earnings expectations as it ramped up production of its new R2 entry-level SUV that the company has promised investors will lead it to profitability.Here's how Rivian performed in the period ended Sept. 30, compared with average estimates compiled by LSEG:Loss per share: 48 cents adjusted vs. loss of 62 cents expectedRevenue: $2.16 billion vs. $1.99 billion expectedShares of Rivian were up roughly 7% during afterhours trading Thursday, after hitting a new 52-week low of $11.38 earlier in the day. The stock closed at $11.45 a share, down 1.9%The electric vehicle maker also revised its 2026 guidance to mark expected improvements in its vehicle deliveries, pre-tax adjusted earnings and capital expenditures.The new guidance calls for a pre-tax adjusted loss of between $1.75 billion and $1.85 billion — a $100 million improvement at the midpoint from its prior guidance — vehicle deliveries of between 67,000 and 70,000 units, up from at least 65,000; and capital expenditures of between $1.4 billion and $1.5 billion, $300 million less at the midpoint.Rivian attributed the improvement in its pre-tax adjusted earnings guidance to better-than-expected revenue related to its sales of regulatory credits, an IEEPA tariff refund receivable in the third quarter and its expected increase in vehicle deliveries.The R2 — the first deliveries of which arrived to customers in June — has become Rivian's best-selling model and was responsible for "much of the gain quarter-over-quarter," the company said. Rivian delivered a record 19,248 units from July through September. The company does not disclose deliveries by vehicle.watch nowThe EV maker remains unprofitable overall but continued to narrow its losses during the quarter. The company reported a net loss attributable to common stockholders of $913 million, compared with a loss of $1.17 billion during the third quarter of 2025.Rivian's gross profit, which is closely monitored by investors, was $176 million during the third quarter, up from $24 million a year earlier. Its adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization was a loss of $435 million, a $167 million improvement from the same period last year.The company reported that its software and services segment continues to grow, generating $605 million in revenue and a gross profit of $256 million, a 42% margin. That compares to its automotive operations, which recorded nearly $1.55 billion in revenue and a gross loss of $80 million.Also on Thursday, Rivian reiterated that it expects the R2, a smaller and less expensive sibling to its current luxury R1S SUV, to have a positive gross margin by the end of the year. CEO RJ Scaringe has said the company needs to scale beyond current R2 production plans of 160,000 units in order to achieve overall profitability."That ramp-up is critical for us getting to positive gross margin on R2 and that ultimately will contribute to positive gross margin for the business," Scaringe told CNBC's Phil LeBeau during an interview Thursday. "We're going to see that through the end of the quarter and the unit economics will continue to grow … into Q1 of next year as well."Rivian on Thursday said its cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments balance was $5.5 billion, up from $5.3 billion to end the second quarter.watch now

title: European Central Bank keeps key interest rate on hold at 2.5%
description: A man walks past the Euro currency sign ('Euro Sculpture' by German artist Ottmar Hoerl) in front of the former European Central Bank (ECB) building i
body: A man walks past the Euro currency sign ('Euro Sculpture' by German artist Ottmar Hoerl) in front of the former European Central Bank (ECB) building in Frankfurt am Main, western Germany, on June 9, 2026. Kirill Kudryavtsev | Afp | Getty ImagesThe European Central Bank voted to hold interest rates steady on Thursday, meeting market expectations, despite euro zone inflation rising to a three-year high. It keeps the central bank's key rate, the deposit facility, at 2.5% following a 25 basis point hike in September. In a statement, the institution's Governing Council said rising energy prices posed upside risks to the inflation outlook and downside risks to growth, but that underlying inflation and wages were so far broadly stable. "At this point in time we are not seeing second round effects in addition to what is already included in the projections" released in September, ECB President Christine Lagarde told CNBC's Annette Weisbach during a press conference. Lagarde identified the main developments since the ECB's last meeting as higher energy costs across oil, petrol, fuel, gas and refining margins, and a sharp rise in long-term financing costs, with the average 10-year sovereign yield up by around 35 basis points."If you combine these two factors — actually, the Governing Council debated whether a hike was appropriate — but on the basis of the uncertainty that accumulates and that rises as well, on the basis of underlying inflation that has broadly remained unchanged, the Governing Council unanimously decided that we were well positioned enough at this stage to hold and that a measured approach at this point in time remained appropriate," Lagarde said. Money markets were pricing in around a 67% probability of a rate hike in December following the announcement, according to LSEG data.Stock Chart IconStock chart iconThe dollar extended gains against the euro in the wake of the ECB decision Headline inflation in the euro area hit 3.8% last month, the highest level since September 2023. Energy price inflation reached 18.8% amid continued turbulence in the Middle East. The resurgence in energy price pressures following the outbreak of the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran in February saw the ECB hike rates in June for the first time since 2023.The euro area economy continued to expand in the third quarter of the year, with a recovery in services since the start of the Middle East conflict, the Governing Council said in an explanation of its decision Thursday.Manufacturing, digital services and exports are being boosted by AI-related investments, while government spending on infrastructure and defense is supporting business activity. However, energy price pressures are likely to hit consumer confidence as higher financing costs weigh on growth.In her press conference, Lagarde said the ECB would continue monitoring rising French borrowing costs and increased fragmentation that has spooked some market watchers. Lagarde noted borrowing costs at the long end of the curve were rising significantly around the world, which she attributed to expectations for inflation and interest rates as well as "debt issuance by some of the hyperscalers," which she said were issuing more long-term bonds and driving up competition. One more hike?"Predicting the path of ECB monetary policy is becoming more challenging," Deutsche Bank's chief European economist, Mark Wall, said in a note on Thursday."One question is whether the two hikes already delivered and the tightening of financial conditions since September are enough to lean against the further increase in energy inflation risk? Probably not."Wall said the other main question was whether the looming departure of Lagarde as ECB president — a decision she announced earlier on Thursday — would impact decision-making next year. "We think the institution is bigger than the person, but there's uncertainty. We expect one more hike to 2.75% in December while Lagarde is still President, and that's probably the end of the hiking cycle."Dean Turner, chief euro zone and U.K. economist at UBS Global Wealth Management, said the Thursday decision "should be viewed as a hawkish pause rather than the end of the tightening cycle." France's fiscal challenge is not expected to change the direction of monetary policy "in the absence of broader financial stress," he said in emailed comments."The ECB's focus remains firmly on ensuring that today's energy-driven inflation does not develop into a more persistent problem."

schema.headline: European Central Bank keeps key interest rate on hold at 2.5%

title: ServiceNow shares plunge 27% to worst day ever after earnings revive AI disruption fears
description: Bill McDermott, CEO of ServiceNow speaks with CNBC on May 5, 2026.CNBCServiceNow shares sank 27% on Thursday and recorded their worst day on record af
body: Bill McDermott, CEO of ServiceNow speaks with CNBC on May 5, 2026.CNBCServiceNow shares sank 27% on Thursday and recorded their worst day on record after the enterprise software company's third-quarter results underwhelmed, reigniting artificial intelligence disruption concerns."This was a little bit uncharacteristic for ServiceNow standards, just in terms of the lack of upside," Citi's Tyler Radke told CNBC on Thursday.Revenue grew more than 20% during the period to $4.11 billion, which was roughly in line with a $4.10 billion estimate from analysts polled by LSEG. Adjusted earnings came up short at $1.00 per share, compared to a forecast of $1.02.The results did little to overturn recent "SaaSpocalypse" fears, or concerns that new AI capabilities will upend traditional software business models.The stock drop came even after the company slightly lifted its full-year 2026 subscription revenue outlook to between $15.78 billion and $15.79 billion. Net new AI average contract value jumped 65%. One factor spooking investors is the lack of immediate payoff for the company's investments in its newly formed forward-deployed engineering team that embeds in enterprises to build AI solutions, Radke said. "It's just going to be a little bit longer of a waiting game, and so I think the market, you know, wanted to see something a little bit sooner," he said. "I think you got to wait until next year to really see that inflection."WATCH: ServiceNow shares plummet in extended trading on mixed Q3 resultswatch nowRead more CNBC tech newsAI build-out hits snag as Google and Microsoft put off raising capex forecastsAlphabet earnings miss reflects first real sign that AI is taking a bite out of searchAs Waymo expands overseas, it remains a niche cash-burning businessHands-on with Apple’s first touchscreen laptop: Touch is totally optional

title: Reddit shares sink on weak sales guidance and plans login requirement test as Google search traffic shrinks
description: Steve Huffman, co-founder and CEO of Reddit, speaks during the WSJ Tech Live conference hosted by The Wall Street Journal at the Montage Laguna Beach
body: Steve Huffman, co-founder and CEO of Reddit, speaks during the WSJ Tech Live conference hosted by The Wall Street Journal at the Montage Laguna Beach in Laguna Beach, California, on Oct. 21, 2024.Frederic J. Brown | Afp | Getty ImagesReddit plans to require all users to create official accounts to access the social media platform, marking a major departure for the site known as "the front page of the internet." The company revealed the change Thursday as part of its third-quarter earnings, in which it beat on the top and bottom lines, but provided weak fourth-quarter sales guidance. The company's shares dropped over 15% after its numbers were released.Here's how the company did compared with LSEG estimates:Earnings per share: $1.40 vs. $1.35 expectedRevenue: $895 million vs. $878 million expectedReddit CEO Steve Huffman told CNBC in an interview that the company's shrinking search-referral traffic from Google went "down meaningfully in this quarter" due to the "shift to AI mode and AI overviews." The traffic decline played a role in Reddit's planned efforts to require people to become logged-in users. A previous Google search update designed to surface "authentic" content from internet forums helped Reddit grow its user base over the past few years, but the search giant's continued push on AI overviews and related chatting features has negatively impacted referral traffic."I think fundamentally that relationship between Google and the rest of the internet is evolving, and so for us, this means a continued focus on our core users that come to Reddit directly," Huffman said.  Previous Google algorithm changes would "kind of come and go," Huffman said, but the company's AI efforts represent "a fundamental shift in how the Google product works, from being a traffic driver to whatever's going on now."Huffman didn't provide any specific timing on when Reddit plans for the platform registration change, saying only that implementing it through the site would involve a lot of complexity. The company will begin testing in the fourth quarter outside of the U.S.He said that Reddit is still determining what parts of the service logged-out users will be able to see, and will iron out the details as part of its upcoming testing.Reddit said that daily active uniques, or DAUq, rose 12% year-over-year to 130.3 million in the third quarter, trailing Wall Street estimates of 133.7 million. U.S.-specific DAUq dropped 2% year-over-year to 50.7 million, which was below analyst projections of 53.5 million.Read more CNBC tech newsAI build-out hits snag as Google and Microsoft put off raising capex forecastsAlphabet earnings miss reflects first real sign that AI is taking a bite out of searchAs Waymo expands overseas, it remains a niche cash-burning businessHands-on with Apple’s first touchscreen laptop: Touch is totally optionalHuffman said that "search referral traffic is down meaningfully in this quarter" and that the trend will continue in the fourth quarter.He said that Reddit is continuing its effort to make its platform "a daily habit" for users. "So that's where our focus is: growing those app users and logged-in users," Huffman said.Reddit, which derives the bulk of its overall sales from online advertising, is able to monetize logged-ln users better than logged-out users, because those registered users are more active and valuable to advertisers itching to deliver more targeted ads."The vast majority of our revenue comes from our app users and logged-in users are direct traffic, and both of those are up Q. over Q. and so that's where our focus is," Huffman said.The company's third-quarter sales grew 53% year-over-year, marking an end to the eight-straight quarters of revenue growth eclipsing 60% that it reported in July as part of its second-quarter earnings.Reddit said that fourth-quarter sales will come in a range of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, which was below Wall Street estimates of $1.05 billion."It's still a strong guide," Huffman said about its revenue guidance. "We are still growing at an industry leading rate, and that's despite the headwinds from search referrals."Reddit's third-quarter average revenue per user, or ARPU, came in at $6.87, which was higher than the $6.50 that analysts were expecting.The company's "other revenue" segment, which includes its data-licensing business, jumped 35% year-over-year to $48 million in the third quarter. Reddit's two biggest data-licensing partners are OpenAI and Google.Huffman said that Reddit remains "in negotiations" with Google over its data-licensing agreement, and said that it is "only going to do a deal that makes sense for Reddit," if it chooses to continue the partnership."I think there's a lot of strategic considerations that goes into that," Huffman said.Huffman called the required registration plan a "big change" for himself, considering he "grew up on the open Internet.""Reddit is the last platform to provide basically unfettered logged-out access, and that's largely because of me, I've been holding that line," Huffman, a Reddit co-founder, said. "I think users will probably go through the same understanding that I have, which is that it's a sign of the times. It's an evolution of how these platforms work."Huffman later expanded on the significance of AI's impact on Reddit's user growth in an earnings call with analysts, and explained that the company plans to continue spending on marketing efforts intended to offset search-referral declines. "This is a consequential time for Reddit, and this period does remind me of about 11 years ago when I came back to the company," Huffman told analysts, referring to when he rejoined Reddit in 2015 following it's then-chief Ellen Pao stepping down. "We had a lot of conversations then about what is Reddit and what is Reddit for, and what is our place in this ecosystem. And we've been having those conversations at Reddit recently." "Reddit's mission is to create community and belonging for everyone in the world, and while there's overlap between Reddit and other players in the ecosystem, whether we're talking about social media or AI search, fundamentally, Reddit is communities and conversations," Huffman said.WATCH: Rotations in the market are likely to continue.watch now

title: Amazon posts negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion, holds 2026 capex unchanged
description: watch nowAmazon shares plunged more than 6% in extended trading Thursday after the company reported disappointing third-quarter results and ballooning
body: watch nowAmazon shares plunged more than 6% in extended trading Thursday after the company reported disappointing third-quarter results and ballooning negative free cash flow, reflecting its swelling AI investments. Here's how the company did, compared with estimates from analysts polled by LSEG: Earnings per share: $1.89 vs. $1.96 estimatedRevenue: $201.94 billion vs. $202.31 billion estimatedWall Street was also looking at other key revenue numbers:Amazon Web Services: $45.98 billion vs. $45.29 billion, according to StreetAccountAdvertising: $19.64 billion vs. $20.82 billion, according to StreetAccountThe company held steady on its capital expenditure forecast for 2026, saying it continues to expect spending will reach $220 billion this year. Tech's hyperscalers have been on a blistering spending run to meet the surge in demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure, but signs have begun to emerge that the capex splurge is moderating. Earlier this week, Microsoft lowered its capex forecast for the year to $170 billion from $175 billion, while Alphabet maintained its guidance at $195 billion to $205 billion. CEO Andy Jassy said on a conference call with investors that the company expects to "spend meaningfully more in 2027," and that Amazon has a "clear line of sight to attractive financial returns." The aggressive AI spending has eaten into Amazon's cash flow. The company posted negative free cash flow for the second consecutive quarter, recording an outflow of $42.4 billion for the trailing twelve month period, a swing of 386% year over year. In the prior quarter, the company reported negative free cash flow of $7.6 billion.The company said the shortfall was primarily due to an increase in purchases of property and equipment as a result of AI investments. Capital expenditures reached $77.3 billion during the quarter, ticking up from $35.1 billion one year earlier, and coming in well above analysts' estimated $58.7 billion, according to FactSet.Amazon said it expects fourth-quarter revenue to be in the range of $240 billion and $247 billion. The midpoint of its guidance was below Wall Street's expectations of $244.5 billion, according to LSEG. The fourth quarter is typically one of Amazon's biggest by revenue, due to the peak holiday shopping season. Sales in Amazon's cloud segment soared 39% year over year to $45.98 billion. That topped the consensus forecast for $45.29 billion and growth of 38%, according to StreetAccount. Read more CNBC tech newsAI build-out hits snag as Google and Microsoft put off raising capex forecastsAlphabet earnings miss reflects first real sign that AI is taking a bite out of searchAs Waymo expands overseas, it remains a niche cash-burning businessHands-on with Apple’s first touchscreen laptop: Touch is totally optionalJassy highlighted AWS acceleration in the earnings release, saying the company expects revenue growth rates of "over 40%" next year and in 2028. He added, "Our AWS investment in functionality and infrastructure is working."Jassy told investors on the call that he expects AWS will be a $1 trillion revenue business in the next five to 10 years. Amazon is facing pressure from Wall Street to show that its AI investments are lifting its revenues. The company pointed to growing traction for Bedrock, its AI model marketplace, along with its Trainium and Graviton AI chips. Jassy said Amazon's chips business "continues to grow triple-digit percentages year over year." He added that the company plans to make its Trainium chips available externally "late in 2027," assigning a timeframe to comments Jassy made earlier this year suggesting such a move.Third-quarter net income came in at $20.69 billion, or $1.89 per share, vs. $21.19 billion, or $1.95 per share, a year ago. The company said the decrease was driven primarily by a $9.5 billion pre-tax gain from its investment in the AI startup Anthropic, which was recorded in the 2025 third quarter.  While the AWS segment continues to hum along, results weren't as bright in Amazon's retail business, which remains its largest unit by revenue, or its advertising segment. Online sales gained 2% year over year to $68.47 billion, which fell short of analysts' projected $69.68 billion, according to StreetAccount. It marked a slowdown from one year ago, when sales increased nearly 10%.Advertising revenue rose 11% year over year to $19.64 billion. That missed StreetAccount consensus estimates of $20.82 billion.Both units were impacted in part by Amazon's decision to pull its annual Prime Day sale forward in several countries from its typical third quarter timeframe into the second quarter so as to not conflict with the FIFA World Cup in July.Stock Chart IconStock chart iconAmazon stock chart.

title: IRS CEO Bisignano donates to Trump Accounts in his childhood Brooklyn ZIP code
description: Frank Bisignano, CEO of the Internal Revenue Service, during a House Ways and Means Subcommittee on Social Security hearing in Washington, June 10, 20
body: Frank Bisignano, CEO of the Internal Revenue Service, during a House Ways and Means Subcommittee on Social Security hearing in Washington, June 10, 2026.Tierney L. Cross | Bloomberg | Getty ImagesIRS CEO Frank Bisignano has donated to Trump Accounts for certain kids in Brooklyn, the agency announced Thursday.The Bisignano Family Fund donated $250 apiece to Trump Accounts of eligible children ages 2 to 8 living in 11234, Bisignano's hometown ZIP code, according to the release. "My life was shaped by the people, schools, and neighborhoods in Marine Park, Mill Basin, Bergen Beach, and Flatlands," Bisignano said in a statement. "This donation is an investment in the children of Brooklyn, giving them a boost in their personal wealth building journeys."Within that ZIP code, fewer than 10,000 U.S. citizens are under 10 years of age, according to CNBC's analysis of the most recent population estimate from the U.S. Census Bureau. The contribution will be invested in a diversified index fund, the release also said. Expanding access to Trump Accounts has been a Trump administration priority. In July, Bisignano was tasked with leading that effort. Read more CNBC personal finance coverageIf Elon Musk gifts SpaceX stock through Trump Accounts, it will come with a catchRoth conversions aren't for everyone. When the 'juice' isn't worth it: Top advisorThe affordability crisis isn't hitting all voters equally. Here's whyMidterm elections: How affordability and the economy could affect voters' decisionsCNBC's Financial Advisor 100: Best financial advisors, top firms for 2026 rankedCNBC Elite Advisors: Top ultra-high net worth wealth management firms for 2026The latest Trump Account news comes weeks after the Treasury Department auto-enrolled more than 60 million children.Trump Accounts, also known as 530A accounts, are open to any U.S. citizen under 18 with a Social Security number. Children born from 2025 through 2028 may also claim a one-time $1,000 pilot program contribution from the Treasury.Families must still activate their child's Trump Account to receive contributions if eligible, according to Treasury guidance.'The tip of the iceberg'Bisignano's commitment comes on the heels of news that Elon Musk plans to give every kid in America a share of SpaceX in 2027.Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner, founder of Invest America and an architect of Trump Accounts, described Musk's gift as "the tip of the iceberg" for philanthropic gifts on CNBC's "Squawk Box" Oct. 21. Gerstner has committed about $35 million to help fund investment accounts for kids in his home state of Indiana.       More gifts are in the pipeline, Bisignano told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Oct. 8. "They range from small to mega," he said. After claiming an account, families can track deposits in the Trump Accounts app, which was designed in partnership with Robinhood."Trump Accounts is direct philanthropy, extremely efficient, direct to children...," Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev said on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on Oct. 28."Excited to see Elon donation," he said. "I think there will be many others as well."watch nowThe Treasury Department in September released temporary regulations allowing Trump Accounts to hold donated individual stocks, a shift from previous guidelines that permitted only diversified, low-cost index funds. The Trump administration said the move could pave the way for more multimillion-dollar donations, with a number of philanthropists poised to participate. The latest donation comes just days before the midterm election, and Republicans fight to keep slim congressional majorities in the Senate and House.

title: Alphabet tanks nearly 13% for worst day ever, losing $500 billion in value
description: watch nowAlphabet shares plunged the most since Google went public in 2004, dropping 13% on Thursday, wiping out roughly $500 billion in market cap. I
body: watch nowAlphabet shares plunged the most since Google went public in 2004, dropping 13% on Thursday, wiping out roughly $500 billion in market cap. In its earnings announcement late Wednesday, Alphabet reported negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion for the third quarter, compared to the $2.7 billion analysts expected. The Google parent maintained its full year capital expenditure guidance of between $195 billion and $205 billion.Microsoft, meanwhile, traded largely flat as investors focused on the tech giants' latest spending and free cash flow numbers in the third-quarter earnings report.Microsoft reported $45.2 billion in capital expenditures and finance leases during the quarter, which was 30% higher than a year ago, but below analyst projections of $50.67 billion. Free cash flow fell 27% to $18.63 billion but remained positive.The earnings reports come as investors scrutinize AI spending plans of tech companies and are focusing on the returns on those investments. "Microsoft is building out its architecture in a measured way and as such contains fewer surprises," Ben Barringer, global head of technology research at Quilter Cheviot, said on Thursday. "Alphabet, by contrast, saw its share price hit after hours as a result of a fairly messy set of results and a poorly handled earnings call" .Read more CNBC tech newsAI build-out hits snag as Google and Microsoft put off raising capex forecastsAlphabet earnings miss reflects first real sign that AI is taking a bite out of searchAs Waymo expands overseas, it remains a niche cash-burning businessHands-on with Apple’s first touchscreen laptop: Touch is totally optionalSearch under pressureAlphabet's biggest source of revenue, search advertising, grew 12% in the September quarter to $63.35 billion, but missed analyst expectations, adding further pressure to the company's shares.Philipp Schindler, Alphabet's chief business officer, said the impact on the search business was partly because of lower monetization within the company's AI Mode. He added that Alphabet is now "scaling" ads within its AI Overviews and AI Mode products, including in international markets. Google's search business has faced headwinds from the rise of other AI chatbots like OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude. People may be carrying out more search queries outside Google. Gemini, Google's own AI chatbot, has failed to keep pace."The problem for Google is it faces an innovator's dilemma and doesn't know whether to protect its core business or look to join the disruption. As such, Google has lost its edge with Gemini and is behind peers on agentic AI," Barringer said.Google's dominant market share in the search business, however, could ultimately give it a leg up over its peers, Rosenblatt Securities analyst Scott Devitt said. "I don't think it's a sea change," Devitt told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on Thursday. "If it's a problem for Alphabet, it's a problem for any consumer-facing AI agent or LLM as well. And so, it's a problem that I think is ultimately going to be resolved. And when it does, Alphabet, with its 4 billion search customers that become AI customers, is in an enviable position."- CNBC's Robert Hum, Samantha Subin, Jordan Novet and Caleigh Keating contributed reporting.

title: Intel stock plunges 21% as chipmaker blames PC slowdown for weak guidance
description: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan speaks during a keynote presentation at Computex in Taipei on June 2, 2026. Cheng Yu-chen | AFP | Getty ImagesIntel shares plumme
body: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan speaks during a keynote presentation at Computex in Taipei on June 2, 2026. Cheng Yu-chen | AFP | Getty ImagesIntel shares plummeted more than 20% in extended trading on Thursday after the chipmaker issued a weak fourth-quarter forecast, citing continued softness in the global PC market.Here's how the company did in the third quarter, compared with estimates from analysts polled by LSEG:Earnings per share: 52 cents adjusted vs. 40 cents expectedRevenue: $16.51 billion vs. $16.5 billion expectedRevenue climbed 21% from $13.7 billion a year earlier, the company said in a press release. However, revenue in Intel's client computing and physical AI group fell 5% from the same quarter a year ago to $8.1 billion, missing estimates, even as data center and AI revenue jumped 78% to $7.3 billion.Global PC shipments declined 4% in the second quarter from a year earlier due to soaring costs for memory and other components, according to Counterpoint Research.For the current quarter, Intel said it expects adjusted earnings per share of 25 cents on revenue between $15 billion and $16 billion. Analysts were expecting revenue of $17.1 billion and EPS of 43 cents, according to LSEG."We see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," Intel finance chief David Zinsner, said in the release. "We will continue making disciplined investments in capacity and working capital to increase supply and support future growth." Intel's forecast reflects the effects of an explosion at a fab in Israel that killed two workers and seriously injured a third earlier this month. The incident will cost the company about $600 million in lost revenue over two quarters, Zinsner said on Thursday's earnings. CEO Lip-Bu Tan said the explosion, which he called an "unfortunate and tragic accident," caused an "extended shutdown" at the plant, impacting shipments of 10-nanometer chips.Intel's stock has been on an upward tear, up about 150% so far this year prior to the earnings report, although it's down roughly 23% in October over growing concern over the size of the artificial intelligence buildout. "We will remain disciplined as we invest, and we will not spend $1 of capital unless we have confidence in the health of our products and process technologies, and clear evidence of customer demand," Zinsner said on the call.Nvidia, which has become the world's most valuable company thanks to its dominance in graphics processing units, or GPUs, is scheduled to report results in mid-November. Advanced Micro Devices, a maker of GPUs and central processing units, or CPUs, reports next week. Known best for its industry-leading CPUs, Intel has been a beneficiary of the rise in agentic AI. While chatbots and large models rely heavily on graphics processors from Nvidia and AMD, agentic applications such as Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots lean on CPUs to help orchestrate tasks and data from a computer operating in the cloud."Despite near term headwinds affecting the broader PC industry, we continue to see robust demand for CPUs and more broadly, for all our computing platforms in the long term," Tan said in the press release.watch nowIntel's foundry business, meanwhile, has struggled to find its footing.Intel is the only U.S.-based manufacturer of advanced logic chips, and is now in high-volume production of its most advanced 18A chip out of its new fab in Arizona, providing an alternative to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Its next fab in Arizona is expected to begin operations by the end of 2028.For now, Intel has no major external customers for its new chips. "We're going to have a couple of customers ready to announce the next two quarters," Tan said on the call, adding that Intel is making "tremendous progress" on its coming 14A chips.The Trump administration took a 10% stake in Intel last year after the company had fallen behind on its 7- and 10-nanometer technologies. Nvidia and Softbank also invested billions in Intel last year.  Tan has taken a more cautious approach to foundry spending than his predecessor, Pat Gelsinger, who launched an ambitious revival of the foundry business. Last week, Intel said crews have installed the first structural truss at its huge Ohio fab that was originally expected to deliver chips in 2025.In September, reports surfaced that the world's leading maker of high-bandwidth memory, SK Hynix may team up with Intel in Ohio to lease some foundry space to make memory chips at the new site. Neither company would confirm any plans. "We continue to evaluate unique and highly differentiated opportunities to accelerate our Ohio build out, and I hope to share more on this in the near future" Tan said on the call.Intel completed a $23 billion equity offering in August. Tech giants have spent trillions of dollars in recent years to meet insatiable demand for AI and the infrastructure needed to support it.Tan said he's "disappointed that we were not able to meet strong customer demand in this quarter." title: Weil, Gotshal & Manges, longtime Wall Street law firm, plans wind down
description: watch nowA management committee of Weil, Gotshal & Manges, the long-time Wall Street law firm, has recommended that its partners wind down operations,
body: watch nowA management committee of Weil, Gotshal & Manges, the long-time Wall Street law firm, has recommended that its partners wind down operations, the firm said Wednesday.The recommendation came after an exodus of partners and the reported end, days ago, of talks with Willkie Farr & Gallagher about a potential merger. Weil, which has about 1,200 lawyers, in 2025 reportedly had more than $2 billion in revenue across multi-national operations."For more than 90 years, Weil, Gotshal & Manges has had the privilege of advising clients on some of their most consequential matters," the firm said in a statement to CNBC. "Following a careful review of strategic alternatives, the Firm's Management Committee has recommended to the partnership that the Firm pursue an orderly wind-down," the firm said. "The partners are expected to vote in the coming days."Weil said that during the wind-down process in coming months, the "firm will continue serving clients with the dedication and excellence that have defined it since its founding and will remain committed to supporting its colleagues."Over the years, Weil had been involved in major bankruptcy filings, including for Lehman Brothers, General Motors and Enron.

schema.headline: Weil, Gotshal & Manges, longtime Wall Street law firm, plans wind down

title: Steve Eisman gets more conservative with portfolio as AI trade nears 'tipping point'
description: watch nowSteve Eisman of "The Big Short" fame thinks the artificial intelligence trade is near a "tipping point," but he's not ready to outright bet a
body: watch nowSteve Eisman of "The Big Short" fame thinks the artificial intelligence trade is near a "tipping point," but he's not ready to outright bet against it yet."I've gotten much more conservative in my own portfolio. We have shorted against the box a whole bunch of our positions, so that our risk is much, much, much lower. But I'm not, like, net short any," he told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Thursday.Eisman's primary concern pertains to the frontier algorithm models, which are exploiting a climate of fear around their technologies, he believes, in order to set up a competitive regulatory moat against more cost-efficient products and to obscure some faltering fundamentals. Bigwigs in the tech industry have issued similar warnings.Anthropic left its latest revenue figures blank in its initial IPO filing, but Eisman believes they will show a significant deceleration from the prior quarter. Other figures in the report point to capital efficiency issue, he said.The ratio of revenue-to-equipment-expense was 2.08 in the second quarter and 1.7 in the third, marking a significant change in trajectory, Eisman said, citing an analysis he'd been given.Yet, Eisman said he was scared to make a definitive bet against the AI trade because of how intertwined it is with the market as a whole, calling it "impossible" for the technology sector to be siloed away from the broader equity market and the rest of the economy."So much of the market is on the other side, and it's still reading tea leaves. I think we're getting closer. I think the numbers from Google scared people," he said.Alphabet's stock tanked after reporting earnings on Wednesday, following a big pullback in its core advertising business as AI queries supplant internet search across its various products.Stock Chart IconStock chart iconAlphabet 5 day.Google executives said Wednesday they were running experiments to figure out what to do about it."It's worth noting the strong growth in AI mode queries had an impact because of the lower monetization we are seeing in AI mode," Philipp Schindler, Google's chief business officer, said. "Our ad experiments have shown promising results."Portions of Anthropic's recently filed S-1 struck Eisman as "extremely negative" in light of the fact that it didn't contain many metrics for the upcoming quarter that would give a clearer picture of the company's financial situation.

schema.headline: Steve Eisman gets more conservative with portfolio as AI trade nears 'tipping point'

title: Norwegian shares surge 13% on earnings beat, guidance raise
description: Norwegian Sky, a 77,104 GT Sun-class cruise ship owned and operated by Norwegian Cruise Line, sails the Tagus River after departure from the cruise te
body: Norwegian Sky, a 77,104 GT Sun-class cruise ship owned and operated by Norwegian Cruise Line, sails the Tagus River after departure from the cruise terminal on Sept. 2, 2025, in Lisbon, Portugal.Horacio Villalobos | Corbis News | Getty ImagesShares of Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings surged 13% Thursday after the company posted better-than-expected third-quarter earnings and raised its outlook for the full year. The cruise line reported third-quarter revenue of $2.95 billion, topping Wall Street expectations of $2.88 billion, according to analyst estimates from LSEG. Net income for the period was $491 million, or $1.07 per share.Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization was $937 million, which exceeded Norwegian's previous guidance of $874 million. Adjusted EPS was $1.12, exceeding previous guidance of 90 cents and outpacing analysts' expectations of 94 cents, per LSEG. Norwegian also raised its full-year guidance, citing its stronger-than-expected third-quarter performance. The company now expects 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $2.55 billion and adjusted EPS of about $1.70. The report said the company's bookings had "improved modestly" since its last report but remain below its optimal range. Norwegian said it will emphasize new marketing strategies, including the launch of a new marketing platform in January. It also said it anticipates that enhancements such as a new waterpark at its Great Stirrup Cay private island will support stronger demand. Also on Thursday, Norwegian announced that Chief Financial Officer Mark Kempa will step down after more than 25 years at the company. Meghan Montana, currently chief strategy officer, will take over the role starting Jan. 1.

schema.headline: Norwegian shares surge 13% on earnings beat, guidance raise

title: Some Polymarket user funds stolen by hackers; exchange referring matter to U.K. authorities
description: The Polymarket midterms 2026 website arranged on a laptop in Forest Hills, New York, Oct. 28, 2026.Gabby Jones | Bloomberg | Getty ImagesSome users of
body: The Polymarket midterms 2026 website arranged on a laptop in Forest Hills, New York, Oct. 28, 2026.Gabby Jones | Bloomberg | Getty ImagesSome users of prediction market platform Polymarket's international exchange had funds stolen from their accounts due to a hack of an unnamed third-party provider. Polymarket has contacted law enforcement and pledged to reimburse any affected trader. It's unclear how many users were impacted. The company's U.S. platform was not compromised.Traders first reported on social media platforms that they were seeing unauthorized withdrawals from their accounts on Thursday afternoon. In response, the company halted trading on its international platform. Polymarket said that it has fixed the issue on its end, and that trading resumed at 3 p.m. ET. It told users later in a chatroom on Discord that users who had less than $10,000 taken from their wallets will have funds restored by Oct. 30, and those with funds greater than that figure withdrawn will have to sign a release form to receive their restoration. A person familiar with the matter told CNBC that the issue stemmed from a hack of DebugBear, a website performance monitoring platform. DebugBear in a post on X said that it was impacted by a security incident on Thursday. The person familiar with the Polymarket outage said that the company referred the matter to U.K. law enforcement, as that is where DebugBear is based. DebugBear didn't immediately respond to a request for comment. An analysis of publicly-available data by two analytics firms — Betting Intelligence and Polysights — provided to CNBC said that an account on Polymarket Thursday withdrew at least $2.7 million across 710 other wallets. 'This is certainly a significant and new form of breach that we've seen on Polymarket," said Dan Zimmermann, the chief intelligence officer at Betting Intelligence. "The timing right before the midterms ...is certainly a wake up call for folks."Polymarket's international prediction market exchange operates as a decentralized finance platform on the Polygon blockchain and is not regulated in the U.S. The disruption comes just days before both the company's international and U.S. exchanges are expected to see heightened volumes during the U.S. midterm elections on Nov. 3. Back in June, a similar incident happened, when Polymarket said a third party vendor had been "compromised" and that the company would refund affected users. Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

schema.headline: Some Polymarket user funds stolen by hackers; exchange referring matter to U.K. authorities

title: Circle, Tether freeze funds impacted by potential Binance 'security issue'
description: Circle signage during the company's initial public offering in front of the New York Stock Exchange, June 5, 2025.Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Im
body: Circle signage during the company's initial public offering in front of the New York Stock Exchange, June 5, 2025.Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty ImagesSeveral crypto firms, including Circle Internet Group and Tether, on Thursday froze roughly $1.8 billion worth of funds tied to a potential hack on cryptocurrency exchange Binance.The world's largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes has not explicitly confirmed that it has suffered an exploit as of writing time. In a social media post, the company said it was investigating "a potential security issue" on its trading platform."Our teams are aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating," a Binance spokesperson said. "Rest assured that user funds are completely safe. Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information."Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire said Thursday evening in a social media post that the company had frozen more than 800 million in USD Coin associated with the incident. USDT stablecoin issuer Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino also said in on X that his firm had frozen more than 1.5 billion of its stablecoin that may have been related to a potential breach. Later, Binance co-founder Yi He said in a statement that the XRP and RLUSD-tied firm Ripple helped halt the movement of $200 million worth of funds linked to the possible attack.  But those frozen funds could represent only a fraction of the ones impacted. Crypto data provider Arkham Intelligence linked nearly $6 billion in digital assets — including bitcoin, ether, solana and various stablecoins — to 55 wallet addresses it has linked to the potential exploit.Arkham identifies, tracks and flags crypto wallets by analyzing publicly available blockchain data. It also solicits tips from its community members.Bitcoin — the most widely followed cryptocurrency in the world — slid more than 3% following the executives' statements, breaking below $80,000. Ether fell nearly 4%, while solana shed about 3%. Shares of Circle also tumbled about 5% in after-hours trading on Thursday.

schema.headline: Circle, Tether freeze funds impacted by potential Binance 'security issue'

title: Third-quarter U.S. GDP increases a better-than-expected 3.4% as September inflation accelerates
description: watch nowThe pace of price increases stepped up in September, keeping inflation well above the Federal Reserve's target, while the economy grew faster
body: watch nowThe pace of price increases stepped up in September, keeping inflation well above the Federal Reserve's target, while the economy grew faster than expected in the third quarter, according to Commerce Department reports Thursday.The personal consumption expenditures price index increased a seasonally adjusted 0.5% for the month, putting the annual inflation rate at 3.6%. The monthly increase was the largest since March but in line with the Dow Jones consensus, while the annual rate was 0.1 percentage point below.Excluding food and energy, the core PCE posted respective readings of 0.3% and 3.1%, in line with the consensus. While the Fed follows both measures closely, officials generally see the core reading as more indicative of longer-term inflation trends.While inflation continued to run ahead of the Fed's 2% target, the Commerce Department also reported that gross domestic product was strong in the third quarter. GDP increased at a seasonally adjusted annualized pace of 3.4%, better than the 3.1% estimate and well ahead of the 2.2% in the second quarter.Also, in September consumer spending proved resilient, climbing 0.5%, a bit below the forecast for a 0.6% gain, while personal income rose 0.2%, compared with the estimate for 0.3%.The reports come the day after the Fed voted to hold its benchmark interest rate in a range between 3.75%-4%. Despite elevated inflation readings, central bank officials insist they can afford to evaluate incoming data before deciding on their next move."The period right in front of us is information rich. There is a lot that's happening in the world. My colleagues and I are keen to take notice of it," Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said Wednesday.However, the data deluge from Thursday shows the Fed could have more work to do.A Labor Department report also released Thursday showed that layoffs remain low. Initial jobless claims edged lower to a seasonally adjusted 194,000 for the week ended Oct. 24, below the estimate for 200,000 and near levels last seen in the late 1960s.Stock market futures were negative following the releases while Treasury yields also fell."Net, net, economic growth is powering ahead despite the uncertainty of geopolitical risks and the damage posed to many sectors of the economy by higher energy costs," said Chris Rupkey, chief economist at Fwdbonds. "The economy was thought to have been a lost cause during much of the current Administration's time in office, but real GDP has bounced back above a 3 percent run rate in Q3 2026 for the first time in a year."Economic growth has been driven by higher levels of investment from the artificial intelligence build-out, as well as high levels of consumer and government spending. Consumer spending rose 3.8% in the third quarter, the same pace as the prior period. Gross private domestic investment soared 19.4%, driven by a 20.9% surge in equipment spending and an 8.4% jump on intellectual property products.Real sales to private domestic purchasers, a proxy that Fed officials use for underlying demand, rose 4.9%, compared with a 4.6% increase in the second quarter.There was some good inflation news for the period: On a quarterly basis, PCE prices rose 2.1% on the headline number and 2.5% for core, down respectively from 5% and 3.3% in the second quarter.September's price increases were driven largely by a surge in energy costs that economists fear could be spreading to other parts of the economy. Gasoline and other energy goods saw a 9.2% rise for the month while energy goods and services broadly jumped 5.4%.At the same time, services prices excluding energy and housing rose 0.4%, and housing costs increased 0.3%.

schema.headline: Third-quarter U.S. GDP increases a better-than-expected 3.4% as September inflation accelerates

title: Cruise companies aim to keep fuel costs down. Their strategies for doing so differ
description: Docked and arriving cruise ships in Cozumel, Mexico.Jeff Greenberg | Universal Images Group | Getty ImagesCarnival, Royal Caribbean and Norwegian Crui
body: Docked and arriving cruise ships in Cozumel, Mexico.Jeff Greenberg | Universal Images Group | Getty ImagesCarnival, Royal Caribbean and Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings posted strong earnings for their most recent quarters despite rising fuel prices. How the leading cruise companies navigate fuel costs boils down to starkly different strategies.Oil prices have skyrocketed since the U.S.-Israel war with Iran began on Feb. 28. Brent crude oil reached a six-month high on Friday, settling at $116.72 per barrel. With no clear end in sight for the conflict in the Middle East, the pressure affecting cruise ships' lifeblood seems poised to last into the holiday travel season and beyond. Both Royal Caribbean and Norwegian practice "hedging," or a strategy of using derivatives to reduce exposure to swings in the price of fuel, to account for sharp increases. Carnival CEO Josh Weinstein, on the other hand, told CNBC in an interview last month that cutting fuel consumption is the best way to avert the effects of expensive fuel."At the end of the day, fuel is an input cost for us. The best thing that we can do to control that cost is to use less," Weinstein said at the time.  Jefferies analyst David Katz told CNBC in an interview that companies that hedge do so primarily to manage the cost of fuel, but also to manage Wall Street expectations and prevent hectic stock trading based on fluctuations in the price of fuel. "When you're public, the Street will trade your stock around based on the price of fuel," Katz said. "The Street's argument is that volatility puts pressure on your multiple." "While it is mathematically most likely true that over the long term it is more expensive," he explained. "The benefit of having less fuel volatility in the model and less trading volatility is [it's] good for your multiple."Despite the potential positives of the strategy, Carnival has maintained the stance it has held since 2019: Cutting fuel consumption works better than hedging.And Carnival's third-quarter earnings report last month suggests the strategy may be paying off. Carnival's 'maniacal' cuttingCarnival beat analysts' expectations on both the top and bottom lines for its most recent quarter and reported an all-time high net income of $1.9 billion. Weinstein told CNBC in an interview on "Squawk on the Street" following the release that the company has been "maniacal" about cutting its fuel consumption, saying it's slashed its unit fuel consumption rate by 26% since 2019. "We estimate we've saved about $700 million in 2026 based on that consumption savings rate going down since 2019," he said. Carnival spent $615 million, or about 7.3% of its revenue, on fuel in the third quarter, according to its most recent earnings release. That's an increase from the $425 million, or 6.7% of revenue, that the company spent on fuel in the fourth quarter of 2025, before fuel prices spiked. Carnival projects its fuel costs will rise to $640 million in the fourth quarter, according to its earnings release. Careful hedgingRoyal Caribbean similarly beat analyst expectations for earnings per share for its third quarter, reported Tuesday. However, it narrowly missed on revenue.CEO Jason Liberty attributed the company's beat in part to its hedging strategy during an interview on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" Tuesday morning. "We're a little bit over 60% hedged here for 2026, and so that's helping insulate us from some of the impacts on the rising fuel costs," he said. "It's obviously still impacting us," Liberty said. "[High fuel prices] evaporated a good chunk of our Q3 earnings beat into the full-year guide. But we're continuing to hedge, and we watch."Royal Caribbean spent about $347 million on fuel in the third quarter, or about 6.2% of its revenue, according to its earnings release. That compares with $293 million, or 6.8% of revenue, spent on fuel in the fourth quarter of 2025, which ended on Dec. 31.The company projects fuel costs will continue to rise to $379 million in the fourth quarter.Liberty pointed out that high fuel prices have not dampened demand from consumers for vacations."It's not that we don't see points of challenges, but really what we've seen is that even in those points of challenges, the consumer comes roaring back," he said.Royal Caribbean reported strong bookings for the third quarter and said reservations for 2027 are already up by a high-teens percentage. Norwegian's continued betNorwegian Cruise Line Holdings beat on both the top and bottom lines for its third-quarter earnings, reported on Thursday, with revenue of $2.9 billion and adjusted earnings per share of $1.12.The company has hedged approximately 48% of its fuel consumption for 2026, according to the earnings release.Norwegian spent about $196 million on fuel in the third quarter, or about 6.6% of its revenue, according to its most recent earnings release. That's a lower share of revenue than the 7.4% — totaling $167 million — spent on fuel in the fourth quarter of 2025, which ended on Dec. 31. The company projects fuel consumption to rise slightly in the fourth quarter, up to 255,000 metric tons from 239,000 metric tons consumed in the third quarter.The company is in the midst of a turnaround effort. And despite facing added challenges from the macro environment, Chief Financial Officer Mark Kempa said he is reassured by this quarter's results on an earnings call on Thursday. "These results reinforce our confidence in the appeal of our products and the opportunity to translate stronger revenue performance and disciplined cost management into improved profitability," Kempa said.

schema.headline: Cruise companies aim to keep fuel costs down. Their strategies for doing so differ
